mainTopic: How settlements join into one city for measuring the תחום שבת: the קרפף, the three villages, and the rules for measuring the תחום.
overview: Background: the תחום שבת is the 2,000-אמה walking limit around a city. רבי מאיר holds that a small extra zone called a קרפף (about 70⅔ אמות) is added to each city before measuring. The גמרא first shows that the משנה's two-city clause also follows רבי מאיר. It explains through a two-way צריכותא why both clauses are needed. Next it tries to refute רב הונא from the משנה about three villages, where a middle village joins the outer two. רב הונא answers with רבי חנינא's reading: the middle village may sit off to the side and is only imagined as filling the gap. רבא and אביי then work out the limits of this rule, comparing it to a bow-shaped city (עיר העשויה כקשת). רב ספרא asks how אקיסטפון and ארדשיר can join across the Tigris, and רבא shows him submerged wall foundations that close the gap. Finally a new משנה begins, teaching that the תחום is measured with a 50-אמה rope at heart level, spanning across canyons, fences and hills.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that each of two neighboring cities gets its own קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who holds the rule just quoted, that a קרפף is given to this city and also to that city. This is a setup question, and the answer comes right away in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving each of two cities its own קרפף means the קרפף is tied to each city, not just to the gap between them. The גמרא wants to know which side of the מחלוקת in the משנה this fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is this?, the standard way to ask which תנא holds a teaching
An extra zone of about 70 and two-thirds אמות added around a city before measuring the תחום שבת

phrases.english: Whose (opinion) is this?
phrases.notes: Refers to the teaching that a קרפף is given to each of two neighboring cities.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by asking who holds the teaching about two cities.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that each of two neighboring cities receives its own קרפף.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the teaching follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that every city gets a קרפף. So when there are two cities, each one naturally gets its own. That fits the teaching that a קרפף is given to each city.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that a קרפף is always given to a city

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: He holds 'we give a קרפף to a city,' so each of two cities gets one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching follows רבי מאיר, who gives a קרפף to every city.

steps.title: Why repeat רבי מאיר's rule?
steps.stepSummary: If this is רבי מאיר, the teaching seems repetitive, since the רישא already quoted him saying a city gets a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי מאיר, he already taught in the first clause: 'We give a קרפף to a city,' these are the words of רבי מאיר. So why say it again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that this teaching looks extra. רבי מאיר's view was already stated in the רישא of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every city gets a קרפף, then of course two cities each get one. So the second statement seems to add nothing new. The גמרא assumes that a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
We give, here meaning we add or allocate
The words of; used to name the author of an opinion

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: Accepting the answer just given.

phrases.english: he already taught it in the first clause:
phrases.notes: Points back to the opening of the משנה.

phrases.english: 'We give a karpef to a city,'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: So why repeat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, הָא תָּנֵי לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by pointing out that it makes the teaching repetitive.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the two-city teaching to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's general rule already covers every city, so stating the two-city case again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The first clause alone would not teach two קרפפות for two cities
steps.stepSummary: The answer is צריכא. From the רישא alone, one might think two cities share a single קרפף. The second clause teaches that each city gets its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If we had only the first clause, I would have said: one קרפף for one city, and also just one קרפף for two cities. So it teaches us that two cities get two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both statements are needed. Here it explains what the second clause adds that the first clause could not teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא only says that a city gets a קרפף. It does not say what happens when two cities are close together. One could have thought they share one קרפף between them, so the second clause teaches that each city gets a full one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; introduces an explanation of why two similar teachings are both needed (צריכותא)
I would have said; the mistaken assumption one might have made (הוה אמינא)
It teaches us; introduces the real new point

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is changing רבי מאיר's opinion here. He always gives a קרפף to a city. The question is only whether two cities next to each other share one קרפף or each get their own.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
phrases.notes: Both statements are needed.

phrases.english: for if (we had learned only) from that one, I would have said:
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the first clause about a single city.

phrases.english: one for one (city), and one for two (cities).
phrases.notes: The mistaken assumption: two cities would share a single קרפף.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that for two (cities) we give them two.
phrases.notes: Each city gets its own קרפף.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי מֵהַהִיא, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by showing what the second clause adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the רישא alone, two neighboring cities might share a single קרפף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two cities receive two separate קרפפות.

steps.title: The second clause alone would not teach a קרפף for one city
steps.stepSummary: The other direction: from the two-city clause alone, one might think the קרפף is given only because two cities are crowded. Then a single city would get none. So the רישא is also needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only here (about two cities), I would think it is because their use of the space is crowded. But there (one city), where their use is not crowded, I would say no קרפף is given. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing the reverse: the first clause is also needed. This closes the answer to the קשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we knew only the two-city case, we might think the reason for the קרפף is crowding, since two populations are using the space between the cities. A single city has no such crowding, so we might have given it nothing. The רישא teaches that even one city gets a קרפף.
steps.whatToRemember: Both clauses of the משנה follow רבי מאיר and both are needed. The single-city clause teaches that every city gets a קרפף even without crowding. The two-city clause teaches that neighboring cities do not share one קרפף; each gets its own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic two-way צריכותא. The גמרא shows that each statement blocks a different mistaken assumption, so the משנה is not repeating itself.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us (only) here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the two-city clause.

phrases.english: (I would say it is) because their use is crowded,
phrases.notes: Two cities share the area between them.

phrases.english: but there, where their use is not crowded,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the single-city case.

phrases.english: I would say not (no קרפף is given),
(therefore) it is necessary.
phrases.notes: Both clauses are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָכָא, מִשּׁוּם דִּדְחִיקָא תַּשְׁמִישְׁתַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 4 by giving the reverse direction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the two-city clause alone, the קרפף might seem to exist only because of crowding, so a single city would get none.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a single, uncrowded city gets a קרפף, so the רישא is also needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both clauses follow רבי מאיר and neither is repetitive.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about three villages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if three villages are lined up and the two outer ones are only 141⅓ אמות apart, the middle village joins all three into one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: Likewise, three villages lined up in a row. If there are only 141⅓ אמות between the two outer ones, the middle village makes all three count as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה to set up a challenge against רב הונא. This step is the setup. The attack itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why 141⅓ אמות? A קרפף is 70⅔ אמות, and two of them add up to 141⅓. At this point the גמרא understands the משנה as describing three villages in a straight line, with the middle one physically sitting between the other two.

phrases.english: We learned: And likewise, three villages that are lined up,
if there is between the two outer ones
141⅓ cubits,
phrases.notes: Two קרפיפות of 70⅔ each

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה אֶמְצָעִי אֶת שְׁלָשְׁתָּן לִהְיוֹת אֶחָד.
phrases.english: the middle one makes all three into one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה כְּפָרִים הַמְשׁוּלָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having finished with the two-city clause, the גמרא makes a new attempt to test רב הונא's view (each of two cities gets its own קרפף) from the משנה's case of three villages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three lined-up villages whose outer two are 141⅓ אמות apart are joined into one by the middle village.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה refutes רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only joins the villages because there is a middle one. Without a middle village they would not join. That seems to refute רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is only because there is a middle village. But if there were no middle village, they would not join. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden implication out of the משנה and uses it to attack רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that each of two cities gets its own קרפף. So two villages 141⅓ אמות apart should join even with no middle village. The משנה implies a middle village is needed, which contradicts him.
steps.confusionAlert: The attack is not based on what the משנה says outright. It is based on what the משנה implies: 'only because there is a middle village.'

phrases.english: The reason is that there is a middle one,
but if there is no middle one, then not.
A refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא אֶמְצָעִי, הָא לֵיכָּא אֶמְצָעִי — לֹא. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that two neighboring cities each get their own קרפף, giving 141⅓ אמות between them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two outer villages needed the middle one to join at 141⅓ אמות, then a double קרפף alone is not enough to join two cities.

steps.title: רב הונא reads the משנה through רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that, according to רבי חנינא, the villages are not really in a row. We imagine moving the middle village between the outer two. If the gaps would then be only 141⅓ אמות, all three join.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: Wasn't it already said about this משנה, in the name of רבה, quoting רב אידי, quoting רבי חנינא: The villages are not literally lined up. Rather, we look at the case this way: if we placed the middle village between them, so that they were lined up, and there would then be only 141⅓ אמות from one to the other, the middle village makes all three into one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself by giving a different reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle village actually sits off to the side, and the outer villages are farther apart than two קרפיפות. The middle village matters only as an imagined 'filler' between them. So the משנה is about villages that are far apart. It says nothing against two villages that really are within 141⅓ אמות joining on their own, which is רב הונא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated about it (an אמורא's explanation of the משנה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading turns the middle village into a measuring tool, not a physical bridge. That leads straight to the next question: how far away can it be?

phrases.english: Rav Huna could say to you:
Wasn't it stated about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Idi said that Rabbi Chanina said:
Not actually lined up,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רוֹאִין כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ מֵטִיל אֶמְצָעִי בֵּינֵיהֶן
phrases.english: rather, we view any case where, if one placed the middle one between them
so that they would be lined up,
and there would be between one and the other

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים אַמָּה וְאַחַת וּשְׁלִישׁ —
phrases.english: only 141⅓ cubits,

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה אֶמְצָעִי אֶת שְׁלָשְׁתָּן לִהְיוֹת אֶחָד.
phrases.english: the middle one makes all three into one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: הָא אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the refutation in step 7 by redefining the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the villages are not physically in a row
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle village physically stands between the outer two, so it is needed to connect them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle village is off to the side and is only placed between the others in imagination. The משנה is about villages too far apart to join alone, so רב הונא stands.

steps.title: רבא asks how far the middle village may be
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks אביי how much distance is allowed between an outer village and the middle village.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: How much distance may there be between an outer village and the middle one?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on רבי חנינא's reading, רבא asks for the limit on how far off to the side the middle village can sit and still join the three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the middle village is only moved in imagination, we need to know whether there is any limit to how far away it can be.

phrases.english: Rava said to Abaye:
How much may there be between an outer one and the middle one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בֵּין חִיצוֹן לָאֶמְצָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up about the case as רבי חנינא defined it in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum distance between an outer village and the off-to-the-side middle village

steps.title: אביי answers: two thousand cubits
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the middle village may be up to 2,000 אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Two thousand אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a limit: up to 2,000 אמות between an outer village and the middle one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 2,000 אמות is the standard תחום שבת distance. אביי ties the limit to that familiar measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Two thousand cubits (the תחום שבת distance)

phrases.english: He said to him: Two thousand cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to 2,000 אמות between the outer and middle village

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי from his own earlier ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: אביי himself agreed with רבא בריה דרבה בר רב הונא that, in a bow-shaped city, we may go beyond 2,000 אמות. So why set a 2,000 limit here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But aren't you the one who said: It makes sense to follow רבא son of רבה בר רב הונא, who said: even more than two thousand אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer with a ruling אביי himself agreed to in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a city shaped like a bow (קשת), we measure from an imagined bowstring, even if the gap is more than 2,000 אמות. If an imagined line can bridge more than 2,000 there, an imagined middle village should be able to do the same here. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
Bow (a bow-shaped city, the background case here)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different people named רבא appear here. The one asking is רבא, אביי's study partner. The one being quoted is a different רבא: רבא son of רבה בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: But aren't you the one who said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: It is reasonable to follow Rava son of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who said: more than two thousand cubits!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's 2,000-אמות answer from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's 2,000-אמות limit for the middle village
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי himself agreed that an imagined line in a bow-shaped city can bridge more than 2,000 אמות. So there should be no 2,000 limit for an imagined middle village either.

steps.title: אביי rejects the comparison to the bow-shaped city
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the bow-shaped city is different because houses connect it. The separate villages have no houses linking them, so the 2,000 limit applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, there are houses. Here, there are no houses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא's challenge from Step 11. He says the bow-shaped city is not a fair comparison to separate villages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a bow-shaped city, a continuous line of houses makes the whole city one unit, so we can go past 2,000 אמות. With separate villages, nothing physically connects the middle village to the outer ones. So each outer village must be within 2,000 אמות, the normal תחום, of the middle village.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There (in the bow-shaped city), there are houses.
phrases.notes: The houses link the whole city into one unit.

phrases.english: Here (with the villages), there are no houses.
phrases.notes: Nothing links the villages, so the 2,000 limit stays.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): connected houses versus separate villages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a bow-shaped city may go past 2,000 אמות, the villages should be allowed to as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Houses make the bow-shaped city one unit. The villages have no houses between them, so the distance to the middle village must stay within 2,000 אמות.

steps.title: רבא asks the distance between the two outer villages
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks אביי how far apart the two outer villages may be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said to אביי: How much distance can there be between one outer village and the other outer village?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. He has asked about the outer-to-middle distance, and now he asks about the outer-to-outer distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 set a limit between each outer village and the middle one. Now רבא wants to know if there is also a limit on the gap between the two outer villages themselves.

phrases.english: And Rava said to Abaye:
How much (distance) may there be between one outer (village) and the other outer one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בֵּין חִיצוֹן לְחִיצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new clarifying question, parallel to Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum distance allowed between the two outer villages.

steps.title: אביי says the outer distance does not matter
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the gap between the outer villages makes no difference. What counts is whether the middle village, if moved between them, would leave gaps of only 141⅓ אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much may there be?! What difference does it make to you? In any case where, if you moved the middle village between them, there would be only 141⅓ אמות between one and the other, they join.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is surprised by the question. He answers that there is no fixed limit between the outer villages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not how far apart the outer villages are. The test is whether the middle village is big enough to 'fill' the space when we imagine it between them. If the remaining gaps are 141⅓ אמות or less, all three join.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make to you?

phrases.english: How much may there be?!
phrases.notes: אביי repeats the question in surprise.

phrases.english: What difference does it make to you?
Any (case) where, if one placed the middle (village) between them,
and there would not be between one and the other
more than 141⅓ (אמות), (they join).

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה יְהֵא?! מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 13 by applying the method from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no fixed outer-to-outer limit. Only the 141⅓ test with the imagined middle village matters.
steps.whatToRemember: The width of the middle village decides the case, not the distance between the two outer villages.

steps.title: Even 4,000 אמות apart? Yes
steps.stepSummary: רבא checks whether the rule holds even when the outer villages are 4,000 אמות apart. אביי says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if they are 4,000 אמות apart? He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tests אביי's rule with an extreme case, and אביי confirms it. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא picks 4,000 אמות on purpose, because רב הונא sets that number as a limit for a bow-shaped city. When אביי says 'yes,' he commits to a position that רבא is about to attack.

phrases.english: And even 4,000 amos?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ אַרְבַּעַת אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limit of the rule in Step 14, and prepares the קשיא in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule apply even at 4,000 אמות?

steps.title: Challenge from רב הונא's bow-shaped city rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב הונא: a bow-shaped city is measured from the imaginary string only if its ends are less than 4,000 אמות apart. So 4,000 should be a limit for the villages too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב הונא say: A city shaped like a bow, if its two ends are less than 4,000 אמות apart, we measure from the bowstring; and if not, we measure from the bow itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's 'yes' using a ruling of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a bow-shaped city, the empty space inside the curve counts as part of the city only if the two ends are less than 4,000 אמות apart. So even a city joined by houses has a 4,000 limit. Separate villages should then surely not join at 4,000 אמות or more.

keyTerms.meaning: A city shaped like a bow
Bowstring (the imaginary line between the two ends)

steps.confusionAlert: Measuring 'from the יֶתֶר' is the lenient option, because the whole empty curve counts as city. Measuring 'from the קֶשֶׁת' is stricter.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say:
A city shaped like a bow,
if there is between its two ends
less than 4,000 amos,
we measure (the Shabbos limit) for it from the bowstring,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו מוֹדְדִין לָהּ מִן הַקֶּשֶׁת!
phrases.english: and if not, we measure for it from the bow!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's 'yes' from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that villages join even when the outer ones are 4,000 אמות apart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a city connected by houses loses the 'string' leniency at 4,000 אמות, then unconnected villages should not join at that distance.

steps.title: אביי: here the middle village fills the gap
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that in a bow-shaped city there is nothing to 'fill' the empty space. With villages, the middle village fills it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, you cannot say 'fill it in.' Here, you can say 'fill it in.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא's challenge by showing that the two cases work in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the bow-shaped city, the empty space inside the curve is just empty, so a distance limit is needed. With the villages, we imagine the middle village moved into the gap. Once it is there, the space is actually filled, so the 4,000 limit does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of joining by a middle village rests on imagining that village physically filling the gap. That is why its distance rules differ from a bow-shaped city.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that joining by an אמצעי is treated as real filled space, not just closeness. This explains the leniency compared to רב הונא's rule.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, one cannot say "fill (it in)."
phrases.notes: Nothing exists to fill the empty curve of the bow.

phrases.english: Here, one can say "fill (it in)."
phrases.notes: The middle village is imagined filling the gap.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לֵיכָּא לְמֵימַר מַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): an empty gap versus a gap filled by the imagined middle village
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bow-shaped city's 4,000 limit should also apply to villages.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle village actually fills the gap, so the villages join at any distance as long as the 141⅓ test is met.

steps.title: The Tigris seems too wide to join two towns
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רבא how אקיסטפון and ארדשיר can share one תחום when the river דגלת separates them by more than 141⅓ אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to רבא: Look at the people of אקיסטפון. We measure their תחום from the far side of ארדשיר. And for the people of ארדשיר, we measure their תחום from the far side of אקיסטפון. But the river דגלת separates them by more than 141⅓ אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא points to a real case that seems to break the rule just discussed. Two towns are treated as one city even though a wide river separates them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that two settlements join into one city only if the gap between them is no more than 141⅓ אמות, which equals two קרפף spaces. In practice, people treated these two towns as one city for measuring the תחום. Yet the river between them is wider than that limit, so the local practice seems to contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A town on one bank of the Tigris (Ctesiphon)
A town on the other bank of the Tigris

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Rava:
Look at the people of Akistefon,
for whom we measure the Shabbat limit
from the far side of Ardeshir,
and the people of Ardeshir's area,
we measure the Shabbat limit for them
from the far side of Akistefon.
But there is the Tigris,
which separates them by more
than 141⅓ cubits?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיכָּא דִּגְלַת דְּמַפְסְקָא יָתֵר מִמֵּאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים וְאַחַת וּשְׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 141⅓-אמה rule to a real local case and finds an apparent contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted practice of treating אקיסטפון and ארדשיר as one city for the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Towns join only if the gap is 141⅓ אמות or less. The river gap here is larger, so the towns should not join.

steps.title: Submerged wall foundations close the gap
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows רב ספרא old wall foundations sunk in the river, which bring the towns within about 70 אמות of each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא went out and showed him the foundations of a wall. They are sunk in the Tigris, about seventy and a fraction אמות from the other town.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by pointing to physical evidence. Part of a town's wall continues under the river and comes close to the other town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gap is not measured from the visible riverbank. It is measured from the remains of the town wall under the water. Those remains are only about 70 אמות from the other town, well within the 141⅓-אמה limit. So the two towns really do join, and the practice is correct.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the river itself is ignored. The towns join because the wall remains are part of the town, so the town actually reaches close to the other side.

phrases.english: He went out and showed him
those foundations of the wall,
which are submerged in the Tigris
at seventy cubits and a remainder.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק, אַחְוִי לֵיהּ הָנָךְ אַטְמָהָתָא דְשׁוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from רב ספרא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction: the real gap is smaller than it looks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gap is the full width of the river, which is more than 141⅓ אמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Submerged wall foundations extend the town, so the true gap is only about 70 אמות and the towns join.
steps.whatToRemember: Towns join for the תחום when the gap between them is within 141⅓ אמות. The gap is measured from the actual edge of the town, even if that edge is hidden under a river.

steps.title: Measure only with a fifty-אמה rope at heart level
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: the תחום is measured only with a rope exactly 50 אמות long, held at the level of the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We measure only with a rope of fifty אמות, no less and no more. And one should measure only at the level of his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rules for the tool and the method used to measure the 2,000-אמה תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rope must be exactly 50 אמות. The reasons for this length will be explained in the גמרא. The person measuring holds the rope against his chest, at heart level. The משנה does not give the reason for this here.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה starts here)
At the level of his heart

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may measure only
with a rope of fifty cubits,
no less and no more.
And he may measure only at the level of his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about how to measure the תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תחום is measured only with a 50-אמה rope, held at heart level.

steps.title: Span across canyons, fences and hills
steps.stepSummary: If the measurer reaches a canyon, fence or hill, he spans across it as if the ground were flat, then continues measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was measuring and reached a canyon or a fence, he spans it and goes back to his measuring. If he reached a hill, he spans it and goes back to his measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains what to do when the ground is not flat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The depth of a canyon and the height of a fence or hill are not added to the 2,000 אמות. Instead, the rope is stretched straight across from one side to the other, as if the area were flat. Then normal measuring resumes on the far side.

keyTerms.meaning: He spans it (measures straight across it)
Goes back to his normal measuring

steps.confusionAlert: Spanning does not mean the obstacle is skipped for free. Its horizontal width still counts. Only its depth or height is not counted.

phrases.english: If he was measuring and reached
a canyon or a fence,
he spans it and resumes his measurement.
If he reached a hill,
he spans it and resumes his measurement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מוֹדֵד וְהִגִּיעַ לְגַיְא אוֹ לְגָדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the measuring tool to uneven ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Canyons, fences and hills are spanned horizontally. Their depth or height is not counted in the תחום.
